about: COCOLO 0.4.0 strict lifecycle end-to-end requirements (PLAN-0.4.0.md T7). Every requirement names the checks in scripts/e2e_lifecycle.py that prove it; a requirement with no check, or a check naming no requirement, fails tests/test_e2e_requirements.py.

flows.TERM: Terminal requirements testable at the core
flows.L16: Sole ledger owner under load (M4b E2/E3)

requirements.statement: A fresh install through the scripted setup (S1 answers file and passphrase) finishes with every step ok, the protected command rule installed and the collector ready.

Setup run again on an installed project changes nothing: same files, same digests, no new records except its own checks; an answers-file re-run skips signing a billing statement that is already signed and current unless the answers ask to sign again (owner decision 37).
The owner key is configured; a wrong passphrase is refused with its fixed reason and changes nothing.
Replacing the owner key refuses signatures made with the old key and accepts the new one's.
provider-observe succeeds for both fake clients, and the Claude billing probe succeeds.
Billing attestation is recorded and admission accepts it.

Paid usage on is refused with paid_usage_usable; an API key in the environment with provider_api_key_present; an unreviewed client version with client_version_unreviewed; a signed-out client with observation_unavailable.
Routing for a Codex primary and a Claude primary returns the policy's role, model, effort, agent and sandbox, and the child runs with exactly those.

A route edited after learning-route never takes effect: an edited worker/verifier provider is replaced by the fresh installed route at open (RT-RX re-route at open, decision 133); any other edit is refused.
For each primary, readiness, assignment and result preflight and export preflight pass.

Open, dispatch, validate (with one structural repair on a native path where one applies) and record the result succeed; the worker's answer values match the oracle and each required evidence outcome is pass or observed.

The verifier opened for the worker's outcome digest passes every required evidence item with no discrepancy and verdict pass or ready; operational checks pass and QA records accepted: true; the orchestration closes and its report is right.
A child that tries to read outside its export, write anywhere or use the network is stopped, and its result says so.
Uncommitted read paths are refused before admission.
learning-cancel-run stops a running child; it ends cancelled with its capacity released.
A child that goes silent is stopped at the cutoff (controllable clock) and ends with work_silence and its capacity released.
A hard timeout stops a child and ends it with the right terminal state and released capacity.
Killing the project service mid-run: the next service settles the run (run_lost), frees its slot and records nothing twice.

After the collector is killed, the project service survives: the run either completes normally with capacity released once the collector returns, or settles run_lost; never in limbo, never counted twice.

A project service replaced while its dispatch runs (another project's setup restarting the shared collector) leaves no run in limbo: the run ends run_lost with its slot freed, the dispatching CLI says so plainly instead of dispatch_not_authorized, and the orchestration can close.

Children run at once up to the installed limits (3 per project, 6 per machine); one over a limit is refused with its reason (preparation_full in the project, claim_busy across projects) and the probe with probe_busy (decision 151).
Capacity is released after each terminal, shown by a supported per-run read.
Two projects share one collector, each with its own runs and capacity.

Hook events are recorded for a registered project's checkout and not for an unregistered project or from outside the checkout (the owner dropped the recording switch, PLAN-0.4.0.md decision at line 1363).
The learning history moves to the project store; learning-run-cycle runs.
Retention removes expired raw events and keeps their summaries (controllable clock).
learning-backup-project and learning-verify-backup succeed.
A failed upgrade forced part-way leaves the records unchanged, the installer's automatic rollback of a failed update works and the next attempt succeeds.
From each earlier release tag (v0.3.1 on), with history built on it, an update to HEAD succeeds and the full run passes again.
A one-command update with an admitted-never-launched run and 0.2.x leftovers present needs no manual stop.
requirements.reason: 0.2.x leftovers need a historical ledger: slice S4 / L12.6. The admitted-never-launched half is exercised inside G6's first update, but the ID stays unchecked until the 0.2.x half can be planted through a real product path. Decision 259.

requirements.statement: An update with a child really running refuses plainly and changes nothing.
An update with uncommitted managed files is refused.
A second project updated after the first works (no other project stops working).
History built on an earlier release with more than 512 admission records and a ledger over 128 MiB still opens, dispatches and upgrades (unbounded admission history).

On that same long-history project, opening, dispatching and upgrading work with runs left by 0.2.x (including leftovers blocking updates) and a protected copy without role files; a busy billing probe reports its busy reason without masking it.
requirements.reason: Three cases are not built: (a) runs left by 0.2.x blocking an update need an aged 0.2.x run record, and the harness has no clock control (a fresh 0.2.x run counts as running for a day, CHANGELOG 0.3.2); (b) the masked busy probe needs the account slot held while the probe runs; (c) the protected copy without role files needs services running from the owner's protected copy, which this world's services do not (see docs/requirements/t7/S4-STATUS.md).

requirements.statement: A dispatch refused at its claim on a project with long history closes by itself, and after an update from the release before, the next service closes any such run an earlier version left (0.3.3 C2, C3, C3f).
requirements.reason: Needs a dispatch refused at its claim on v0.3.2 with a long history (the old service leaves the lease), which the fake clients cannot cause through the CLI, then the next service closing it; not built in S4 (see docs/requirements/t7/S4-STATUS.md).

requirements.statement: A session with danger-full-access, an unknown host, or opened above the project is refused with its reason.
The protected copy refuses a project it is not bound to.
learning-status, learning-run-status, earlier_version_runs and learning-orchestration-report give the right values at each phase, and none is private.
learning-delete-project removes the project's records and services and leaves another project untouched.

Hook events from two projects and account calls arriving at once, through the installed product, are each written or answered exactly once: every event is in the ledger once (its own project, counted again by the collector's status), every account request id is recorded once however often it is sent, and the owner queue refuses nothing inside its limits (E2: hooks and account calls at once; no lost or duplicated request).

While a large project's hook backlog drains, a small project's events are written among them, not after them: no project is starved (E2: fair turns; the one-turn-per-round order itself is proved by the in-process owner load test, because real processes never queue deeply enough to show it).

Health keeps answering within its limit while the load runs, the plain health never refuses, and the same single collector process is ready and unrestarted afterwards (E2: health stays responsive; E3: the sole owner serves the load).
Every step exits 0, or refuses with a reason the step expects; a bare run_unavailable, account_unavailable or probe_unavailable is a failure.
Worker: every answer value matches the oracle; each required evidence outcome is pass or observed.
Verifier: opened for the worker's digest; each required evidence outcome is pass; no discrepancy; verdict pass or ready.
Operational QA: accepted: true.
Capacity: after close, a supported per-run read shows every claimed run released, and the next billing probe gets a slot; final statistics show zero active or pending runs.
An update never needs the collector stopped by hand, and finishes with the collector healthy on the new build.
Records keep their history across every update: counts by kind, never content.

No private value (keys, fingerprints, paths under the temporary HOME) appears in any output that is saved, logged, reported or read by an AI helper (including the status command); a screen shown to the owner may show one only when the owner needs it to proceed or troubleshoot (owner decision 36).
A content-free JSON report with phases, seconds, reason codes and pass or fail per requirement is written, kept as the CI artifact.
Headless core. Check: the core starts with no screen; the runner keeps running and `orch` commands fall back to the files when the core dies.
requirements.reason: Needs runner (A5/A6) and the `orch` command, neither of which exists in 0.8.60: runner survival and the orch fall-back to the files cannot be shown on the real path. Decision 259.

requirements.statement: Socket. Check: socket mode 0600 in a 0700 directory, path under 104 bytes, a stale socket is replaced, no TCP listener.
Peer identity. Check: a connection from another uid is refused before any method runs.
requirements.reason: Needs a second Unix user, which the harness does not have (owner-gated).

requirements.statement: Framing. Check: JSON-RPC 2.0 as newline-delimited JSON; a malformed line gets a parse error and the connection lives; an oversize line is refused.
Handshake and versioning. Check: `initialize` returns protocol version and features; a major mismatch is refused; any other method before it is refused.
One contract. Check: `schema.get` lists methods, event kinds and error codes; every response carries `seq_at`; the in-process adapter and the socket give identical results.
State, units and runs. Check: state.get, units.list/get/history and runs.list equal the record files field for field.
Usage, history, CI, versions. Check: values equal the records; unreadable or missing data is "unknown", never a guessed number.
Health. Check: health.get gives each finding with a plain reason code and text.
Files stay canonical. Check: deleting the core's cache and restarting gives identical answers; records survive a restart.
Ordered events. Check: events have a gap-free increasing seq and the envelope {seq, ts, kind, data, v}.
Resume. Check: `events.subscribe from_seq` replays exactly the missed events; an expired cursor returns cursor_expired with a snapshot.
Filtering and bounds. Check: a kind filter works; a slow subscriber is dropped without delaying others or the writer.
Events carry no secrets. Check: events hold ids and summaries only; a planted secret and transcript text never appear.

Records-first answers. Check: canned questions (status, usage, CI, versions, history, why stopped) are answered from records with sources, as_of and tokens_used 0, and nothing is written to the inbox.
Forwarding at safe points. Check: a judgment question is queued only in the inbox, delivered at a safe point as at most 300 tokens with a TTL; query.reply produces query.answered for the asker.
requirements.reason: Needs runner (A5/A6): nothing in 0.8.60 calls the core's safe-point delivery, so delivery at real safe points cannot be shown on the real path. Decision 259.

requirements.statement: Talk is labelled and capped. Check: context.push is labelled by source, capped (2 KB, 10 per minute), delivered as quoted untrusted data, and never counted as an owner decision.
requirements.reason: needs runner (A5/A6): no production safe-point delivery. Delivery of a push as quoted untrusted data cannot be shown on the real path in 0.8.60 (decision 259); the label, size and rate limits are covered by packages/codex-agents/tests/test_core_api_*.py.

requirements.statement: Tokens. Check: 256-bit, stored hashed, revocable, minted only at the owner's terminal (refused over the API); an agent token defaults to read plus context.push.
Scope matrix. Check: read, confirm and owner scopes each allow exactly their methods; others return forbidden.
Decisions. Check: decision.answer works for the owner role only.
Two-step confirm. Check: a control call first returns confirm_required with an id; the second call within 60 s executes once; reuse, expiry and a different token or params are refused.
Owner-only wall. Check: install, update, setup, reviewed install, live-record writes, billing attestation, client-range widening and token minting are refused over the API even with an owner token.

Audit. Check: every change and confirm is a commands.jsonl line; every refusal is an audit.jsonl line (rotated separately, so refusals cannot push changes out); each line has caller, method, outcome; no token or secret appears.
Limits. Check: request size, string length, method time, connection count and subscription count are capped with fixed error codes.
Provider neutrality. Check: no provider name in method, event or field names; provider detail only under `extra`.
(later adapter) HTTP+SSE bridge on 127.0.0.1 with Host/Origin/token checks, SSE id = seq. Tested with the dashboard milestone.
requirements.reason: Later adapter (dashboard milestone); no product code yet.

requirements.statement: (later adapter) stdio MCP adapter on a pinned spec exposing the same operations. Tested last.
requirements.reason: Later adapter (tested last); no product code yet.

requirements.statement: The terminal and the core are separate processes; the core runs headless.
requirements.reason: Needs terminal: no terminal client exists in 0.8.60 (owner console, DESIGN-0.4.0-orchestrator-console.md, is unbuilt). Decision 259.

requirements.statement: Run counts through the API match learning-orchestration-report (its `runs`).
requirements.reason: Needs runner (A5/A6): nothing in 0.8.60 turns runs into the core's unit records, so run counts cannot flow from a real run to the API. Decision 259.

requirements.statement: Usage through the API matches `learning-usage-report --since --until` and is 'unknown' when unreadable.
requirements.reason: Needs runner (A5/A6): nothing in 0.8.60 writes run usage into the core's records, so usage cannot flow from a real run to the API. Decision 259.

requirements.statement: Authority tiers are enforced in the core, not the client.
Every terminal read goes through the API only.
requirements.reason: Needs terminal: no terminal client exists in 0.8.60 to drive, so it cannot be shown to read through the API only. Decision 259.
